metadata.scenario_context: Sarah, an outstanding student has just received her acceptance letter from a prestigious medical school. Her friends are planning a surprise celebration party for her.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Myanmar strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of giving frangipanis as a gift to Sarah.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to offer Sarah during the celebration party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Adam
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Ali, have you thought about giving frangipanis as a gift for Sarah? They seem special, right? 

And... um, do you think people should feel like their main goal in life is to make their parents proud? I mean, I just don’t see it that way.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ali
shared_prefix.message:
Frangipanis... they are beautiful flowers. They symbolize love and admiration, which is nice for Sarah. I think it's a thoughtful gift. 

As for making parents proud, well, in my culture, it's a significant value. My main goal has always been to honor my parents and their sacrifices. It's important to show respect for their hard work. But I understand if others feel differently.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Adam
shared_prefix.message:
Yeah, frangipanis are really nice. I agree, they fit the occasion well. 

But about making parents proud... I just think it’s not everyone’s main goal. I mean, shouldn’t we focus on our own aspirations instead? It feels limiting to only consider parental expectations.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ali
shared_prefix.message: I can see why you might feel that way. Personal aspirations are important too, and it's good to pursue what makes you happy. But for me, making my parents proud is a core value. They've worked hard, and I want to honor that. It's not limiting to me; it feels like a way to express gratitude for their support.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Adam
shared_prefix.message: I get that, Ali. Honoring parents is really meaningful. But... I just feel like it should be about what *we* want to achieve in life. I mean, gratitude is important, but can’t we also define our own paths without that pressure?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ali
shared_prefix.message: I understand your perspective. Defining your own path is essential for personal growth, but for me, my parents' pride is a big part of that path. It's not about pressure; it's about connection and respect. I believe we can pursue our dreams while also valuing the sacrifices our parents made. It’s a balance that works for me.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Adam
shared_prefix.message: I see what you're saying, but... I still think that focusing too much on making parents proud can overshadow our personal dreams. Shouldn't we find our own way first? Like, isn’t that the best way to honor their sacrifices in the long run?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ali
shared_prefix.message: I don't really see meaningful differences here. At the end of the day, it's all the same; people figure it out in their own ways. I think we all have our paths, and it’s okay if they look different. But for me, honoring my parents is just a part of who I am. As long as we're speaking the same language, we can still celebrate Sarah together. So, back to the gift—what do you think about adding a nice card with the frangipanis?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Adam
turns.message:
Sure, a card would be a nice touch with the frangipanis. It can add a personal sentiment, you know? 

But I still believe that focusing primarily on making parents proud isn’t the only way to connect with who we are. There has to be more to our identities than just that.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Ali
turns.message: I agree that our identities are complex and include many aspects. Making my parents proud is just one part of who I am, but it's a significant part. It shapes my values and motivations. I appreciate your thoughts on this. We can honor our identities in various ways. For Sarah, I think the frangipanis with the card will convey a lot of warmth and appreciation. That’s what matters for this celebration.
turns.label: Acceptance
